content.value_statement: Teams often ship generic AI tools that are costly and hard to defend. This skill guides focused AI products with prompts, controls, pricing, and reliability.
actual_capabilities: Explains an AI product stack from user input to validated response.
Shows prompt template patterns for reusable product workflows.
Compares model choices by cost, speed, quality, and use case.
Describes output parsing, validation, retries, and fallback models.
Outlines token tracking, cost calculation, and usage limits.
Names common AI wrapper anti-patterns and safer alternatives.
limitations: The skill does not validate live provider pricing or current model availability.
It does not deploy production services or manage API credentials.
Examples are instructional and need security review before reuse.
It cannot guarantee product-market fit or legal compliance.

use_cases.title: Shape an AI SaaS concept
use_cases.description: Turn a broad AI idea into a focused workflow, audience, output, and pricing risk model.

use_cases.title: Specify product prompts
use_cases.description: Define prompt inputs, output rules, validation checks, and fallback behavior for a user-facing feature.

use_cases.title: Plan cost controls
use_cases.description: Map token tracking, usage limits, model choices, and cost-reduction options before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Map the AI Product
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me define a focused AI wrapper product for [audience]. Include the job, user input, AI role, output, validation, and pricing risk.

prompt_templates.title: Design Prompt Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a product prompt strategy for [workflow]. Include system guidance, user input fields, output rules, validation checks, and retry behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Cost Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Estimate the cost model for [AI feature]. Cover model choice, token limits, usage metering, cache options, plan limits, and margin risks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Defensibility
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my AI wrapper concept for weak differentiation. Identify workflow integrations, data advantages, UX constraints, quality controls, and reasons customers would pay.

output_examples.input: Need a product architecture for an AI email assistant.
output_examples.output: A concise architecture covering input validation, prompt context, provider call, response validation, usage tracking, and user-friendly editing.

output_examples.input: Need to reduce AI API spend for a high-volume feature.
output: Use a cheaper default model for routine requests.
Limit output length by plan and workflow.
Cache repeated requests and track cost per user.

output_examples.input: Need to identify weak points in an AI wrapper idea.
output_examples.output: A review of thin-wrapper risks, missing workflow integration, weak output validation, unclear pricing margin, and limited customer defensibility.

best_practices: Start with one specific workflow and one clear customer segment.
Validate AI outputs before showing them to users or downstream systems.
Track token usage, cost, latency, and quality for every core feature.
anti_patterns: Shipping a generic chat interface without workflow-specific value.
Ignoring provider costs until usage grows and margins break.
Trusting raw model output without parsing, validation, or fallback behavior.

faq.question: What type of products is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is for focused products that use AI APIs to solve a specific user workflow.

faq.question: Does it write production application code?
faq.answer: It provides architecture and implementation guidance, but examples need normal engineering review.

faq.question: Can it help choose between AI models?
faq.answer: Yes. It frames model choice around cost, speed, quality, and task complexity.

faq.question: Does it include cost management guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers token tracking, cost calculation, usage limits, caching, and pricing margin.

faq.question: Is it useful for prompt engineering?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on product prompts with structured inputs, output rules, and validation.

faq.question: Does it replace legal or security review?
faq.answer: No. Teams still need security, privacy, and compliance review before launch.
